holidays.name: National Milk Day
holidays.description: A day to raise a glass of the white stuff and toast the humble dairy beverage. Cookies are strongly encouraged as a dunking companion.
holidays.origin: Commemorates the date in 1878 when milk was first delivered in glass bottles, a milestone often credited to Dr. Alexander Campbell of New York.
holidays.funFact: Glass milk bottles dramatically improved sanitation over the old practice of ladling milk from open cans into customers' pitchers.

holidays.name: National Hot Toddy Day
holidays.description: A cozy salute to the warm, whiskey-spiked sipper made with hot water, honey, lemon, and spices. Perfect for the chilly depths of January.
holidays.origin: Hot toddies have roots in 18th-century Scotland, and the drink is thought to have evolved from the Indian beverage 'taddy'. The unofficial day was created for fans of winter comfort drinks.
holidays.funFact: Many people swear by hot toddies as a cold remedy, though doctors say the main effect is feeling cozy and sleepy.

holidays.name: Step in a Puddle and Splash Someone Day
holidays.description: A mischievous unofficial observance encouraging people to stomp in puddles and gleefully splash a friend. Rain boots recommended, forgiveness required.
holidays.origin: This lighthearted unofficial holiday sprang up in the novelty calendar world, celebrating the childlike joy of puddle-jumping in the dreary winter months.
holidays.funFact: Puddle-jumping is a go-to activity for toddlers, and researchers who study play note that such unstructured physical play supports mood and creativity.

holidays.name: National Human Trafficking Awareness Day
holidays.description: A serious awareness day, included here for balance among the silliness, encouraging people to learn the signs of human trafficking and support survivors.
holidays.origin: Designated by the U.S. Senate in 2007, it kicks off National Slavery and Human Trafficking Prevention Month in January.
holidays.funFact: People often wear blue on this day as a symbol of solidarity, and the National Human Trafficking Hotline in the U.S. is 1-888-373-7888.

holidays.name: Cheese Pizza Day (unofficial January observance)
holidays.description: A day for pizza lovers to celebrate the purest form of the pie, with no toppings to hide behind, just bubbly cheese and a crisp crust.
holidays.origin: Food-calendar enthusiasts created this pizza observance, which often gets lumped in with the January lineup of comfort foods.
holidays.funFact: The classic Margherita pizza is said to have been created in Naples in 1889 and named for Queen Margherita of Savoy.
